messages:
michelle: FYI customer (Clinova) opened a Sev2 — intermittent 403s on Dedicated VPC cluster when calling Redwood API. They say it started ~30m after we rolled edge-lb v2.3.4. Request looks fine at their LB but backend sometimes sees no Authorization header. Repro steps attached below.

michelle: Repro curl they ran (sensitive token redacted):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_OPAQUE" "https://private-clinova.redwood.internal/v1/models/gpt-final:predict"
```

support-bot: Ticket #CNV-2091 created and escalated to customer-success + eng-infra. Please triage.

jonah: Can you paste an edge/ingress trace id and an example request/response pair (raw headers)? Need to see whether header is stripped by LB or by our gateway. Also any pattern (time of day, pod restarts, rollout windows)?

michelle: Trace id from customer: trace=clinova-9a2b. They sent this upstream log from their NGINX LB -> shows header present: 
```
> GET /v1/models/gpt-final:predict HTTP/1.1
> Host: private-clinova.redwood.internal
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_OPAQUE
> User-Agent: Clinova-Client/1.2.3
```
But backend pod (our dedicated gateway) logs show: 
```
2026-02-28T15:02:17.123Z request_id=clinova-9a2b path=/v1/models/gpt-final:predict status=403 auth_header="-"
```
So header present at LB, missing at pod.

raj: Two quick guesses: 1) LB or internal ALB doing redirect/302 to SSO endpoint and strip Authorization on redirect. 2) Istio/Envoy filter (ext_authz or header_whitelist) not passing the header through to the upstream cluster for some routes. Both can be intermittent depending on route matching or cookie-based routing.

elaine: @raj + @michelle this looks like an ext_authz policy that was recently tightened in the edge-lb rollout. We have an Envoy filter that drops non-whitelisted request headers before ext_authz runs. If the whitelist variable was accidentally left empty for the vhost that Clinova is hitting, Authorization will be removed. Example of the problematic fragment we found in staging: 
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: edge-authz-whitelist
spec:
  configPatches:
    - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER
      match:
        context: GATEWAY
        routeConfiguration:
          vhost: "private-clinova.redwood.internal"
      patch:
        operation: MERGE
        value:
          name: envoy.filters.http.header_to_metadata
          typed_config:
            "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.header_to_metadata.v3.Config
            request_rules: []   # <-- empty => strips all non-required headers
```

raj: That matches the timing of the edge-lb roll. If header_to_metadata rules are empty, the filter can act oddly depending on how it was merged — intermittent depending on which gateway replica handles the request.

michelle: Repro script I ran from our side to show LB->gateway packet: 
```bash
# from a jump host to LB
printf 'GET /v1/models/gpt-final:predict HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: private-clinova.redwood.internal\r\nAuthorization: Bearer TESTTOKEN\r\n\r\n' | openssl s_client -connect lb.clinova.example:443 -quiet | sed -n '1,120p'
```
Result: LB forwarded Authorization. Then I port-forwarded to pod and replayed same packet and pod saw header missing. So loss happens between LB and gateway (our side).

infra-bot: rollout-bot: edge-lb v2.3.4 completed at 2026-02-28T14:40:03Z on cluster-dedicated-01.

raj: Immediate mitigation options: 
- quick patch: inject Authorization into a custom header in the gateway ingress (Envoy Filter) so downstream services always receive x-forwarded-authorization.
- rollback: route customer to pre-v2.3.4 gateway (we can pin Clinova to old gateway for a few hours).
- proper fix: update EnvoyFilter patch to whitelist Authorization header and add E2E tests to prevent empty request_rules merges.

elaine: For ext_authz specifically, we can add `include_request_headers: ["authorization"]` to the authz policy. Example snippet: 
```yaml
ext_authz:
  check_settings:
    context_extensions: {}
    include_request_headers: ["authorization"]
```
This will ensure the header is forwarded to the external auth service and not stripped out.

jonah: Can you try the quick patch (inject x-forwarded-authorization) in stage and confirm? If that fixes it, we'll roll to prod and document as emergency mitigation. Also need to confirm no sensitive-token-logging risk (mask headers).

michelle: Applied a temporary filter in staging that copies Authorization -> x-forwarded-authorization and masks logs. Re-tested with Clinova token and staging pod sees header consistently now. Customer confirmed fewer 403s during their load test.

raj: Created PR #infra/edge-authz-214 that: 1) fixes the empty request_rules merge, 2) adds explicit whitelist for Authorization, 3) adds unit test for EnvoyFilter merges. Plan to ship to canary tomorrow morning.

michelle: Clinova accepted temporary routing to pre-v2.3.4 gateway as fallback while we patch. They've scheduled a low-traffic window tomorrow to switch.

elaine: Action items: @raj open follow-up to add smoke-test that exercises Authorization header preservation across gateway deployments; @jonah review PR; @michelle coordinate customer cutover.

jonah: Thanks everyone. Please add links to logs/traces in the ticket. I'll monitor for regressions. :thumbsup:

michelle: Closing loop here — workaround confirmed, PR filed, customer happy for now. Will update ticket CNV-2091 with timeline. :white_check_mark:
